title: Old-Time Leek Storage
subtitle: 1917 USDA Wisdom
items: Leave tops on, shake off soil
Or mulch deep in the row
desc: Old-time leek storage inspired by USDA Farmers' Bulletin 879, Home Storage of Vegetables (1917), rewritten for today: dig leeks with roots attached, stand them upright in moist sand or soil in a cool root cellar, or mulch them deeply right in the garden row for fresh leeks for soups all winter.

title: Gifts for Gardeners Under $15
subtitle: Small Gifts They'll Use
desc: Budget Christmas gift ideas for gardeners and homesteaders under $15: an old-fashioned almanac, hand cream for working hands, a mushroom grow kit, an herb seed kit and a good pair of pruning shears. Great stocking stuffers for anyone who loves the garden. (Contains affiliate links.)

title: Keep Kale Going Into Winter
subtitle: Harvest Through the Cold
items: Add row cover on cold nights
desc: How to keep harvesting kale into winter: light frost makes the leaves sweeter, mulch around the stems, cover plants with row cover on cold nights, pick outer leaves first and wait until frozen leaves thaw before cutting. An easy beginner vegetable garden tip for fresh greens in late fall.

title: Pressure Canning Starter Checklist
subtitle: What You Need to Begin
desc: Pressure canning starter checklist for beginners: a pressure canner with a weighted or dial gauge, jar lifter, canning funnel, mason jars with new lids, a headspace tool and a book of tested recipes like the USDA Complete Guide to Home Canning. Have dial gauges checked for accuracy every year. (Contains affiliate links.)

title: How to Can Cranberry Sauce
subtitle: USDA Water Bath Method
desc: How to can whole cranberry sauce for Thanksgiving using the USDA Complete Guide to Home Canning: boil sugar and water, add cranberries and cook until the skins burst, fill hot jars with ¼-inch headspace and process pints or quarts 15 minutes in a boiling water bath at 0–1,000 ft, adding time at higher altitudes. Homemade holiday sauce ready on the shelf.

title: Gifts for Canning Lovers
subtitle: Thoughtful Gifts Under $35
desc: Gift ideas under $35 for someone who loves canning and homesteading: a canning tool kit, a trusted home canning book, a harvest basket, an heirloom seed vault and a garden tool set with tote. Practical Christmas gifts for preservers and gardeners. (Contains affiliate links.)

title: Keep Hens Laying in Winter
subtitle: Old Poultry Know-How
items: Light to about 14 hrs a day
Gather eggs often in the cold
desc: How to keep backyard chickens laying in winter, based on old USDA poultry bulletins: add light so hens get about 14 hours a day, feed a complete layer ration instead of scratch, offer oyster shell and grit, keep water unfrozen and collect eggs often. Expect a pause during the fall molt.

title: No-Cook Foods for an Outage
subtitle: Eat Well Without Power
desc: No-cook foods to stock for a winter power outage: peanut butter and crackers, canned tuna or chicken, ready-to-eat canned beans, dried fruit, nuts and shelf-stable milk, plus a manual can opener. A simple self-sufficient emergency pantry for storms and blackouts.
